h: The Rest and Work of Shabbat

p: בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פד, ג):
— In Midrash Rabbah at the beginning of this parashah (Bereishit Rabbah 84:3):
"'לֹא שָׁלַוְתִּי' – מֵעֵשָׂו, 'וְלֹא שָׁקַטְתִּי' – מִלָּבָן, 'וְלֹא נָחְתִּי' – מִדִּינָה, 'וַיָּבֹא רֹגֶז' (אִיּוֹב ג, כו) – בָּא עָלַי רָגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף";
— "'I was not at ease'—from Esau; 'neither had I rest'—from Laban; 'neither was I quiet'—from Dinah; 'yet trouble came' (Job 3:26)—the ordeal of Joseph pounced upon me";
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב קוֹדֶם לָזֶה: שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ יַעֲקֹב לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה וְכוּלֵי.
— which connects to the preceding statement: that Jacob sought to dwell in tranquil peace, etc.

The total of this is the total of that, but he will not get anything from him, and in that way he makes a mockery of the one receiving the lashes. ‘He mocks at the undoing of the innocent’ (Job 9:23) – Rav Aḥa said: When the righteous live in tranquility and seek to live in tranquility in this world, the accuser comes and accuses them. He says: Is what is prepared for them in the World to Come not sufficient for them, that they seek to live in tranquility in this world? p: וְהוּא, שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ שֶׁהָיָה נִשְׁלָם בֶּאֱמֶת,
— And the explanation is: Jacob our father was truly perfected in righteousness,
וְעוֹד מִבֶּטֶן אִמּוֹ נִמְשַׁךְ לַהַקְּדוּשָּׁה,
— and from his mother's womb was drawn toward holiness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת סג, ו):
— as written in Bereishit Rabbah (63:6):
בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהָיְתָה עוֹמֶדֶת עַל בָּתֵּי כְּנֵסִיּוֹת וּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת יַעֲקֹב מְפַרְכֵּס לָצֵאת;
— whenever Rebecca passed houses of prayer and study, Jacob agitated to come forth;
וְהָיָה נִדְמֶה לוֹ שֶׁיָּכוֹל לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא לְנֶגְדּוֹ שׁוּם צַד מִבְּחִינַת הַהֵיפֶךְ,
— and it seemed to him that he could dwell in tranquility without facing any manifestation of the opposing side;
וְלֹא עָלָה בְּיָדוֹ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁהָיָה נִרְדָּף מִפְּנֵי עֵשָׂו.
— yet this did not materialize, seeing that he was pursued by Esau.
וְאַחַר זֶה הָיָה נִדְמֶה לוֹ שֶׁיִּשְׁקוֹט, וּבָא עָלָיו צָרַת לָבָן, וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "וְלֹא שָׁקַטְתִּי מִלָּבָן".
— And afterward he thought he might rest, yet the distress of Laban befell him, which is: "neither had I rest—from Laban."
"וְלֹא נָחְתִּי" – הַיְינוּ בְּעֵת שֶׁבָּא יַעֲקֹב שָׁלֵם לִשְׁכֶם,
— "Neither was I quiet"—this was when Jacob arrived whole at Shechem,
דִּכְתִיב: "וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לג, יח), שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עט, ו) שֶׁבָּא עַל קְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא יוֹם מְנוּחָה;
— where it is written: "and he encamped before the city," which the Midrash expounds as entering the sanctity of Shabbat, the day of rest;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "וְלֹא נָחְתִּי", שֶׁגַּם מְנוּחַת שַׁבָּת לֹא הוֹעִיל לוֹ,
— and concerning this he said: "neither was I quiet," for even the rest of Shabbat did not bring final peace,
שֶׁעִם כָּל זֶה בָּא עָלָיו אַחַר כָּךְ צָרַת דִּינָה, וְהֶרְאוּ לוֹ בָּזֶה שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִשְׁלָם עוֹד.
— since immediately afterward the tragedy of Dinah erupted, showing him that the rectification was not yet complete.

p: וְאַחַר כָּל זֶה: "וַיָּבֹא רֹגֶז" –
— And following all this: "yet trouble (rogez) came"—
שֶׁהוּא עִנְיַן חֲרָדָה גְּדוֹלָה הַמַּרְגִּיז וּמַפְחִיד לֵב הָאָדָם –
— referring to an immense, trembling terror that shakes man's heart—
זֶה רָגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה לוֹ בָּזֶה שֶׁכְּבָר אָבְדָה תִּקְוָתוֹ מִכֹּל וָכֹל;
— this was the ordeal of Joseph, wherein it appeared to Jacob that his ultimate hope was entirely lost;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי אֵרֵד אֶל בְּנִי אָבֵל שְׁאֹלָה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, לה),
— as it is stated: "For I will go down to the grave (she'olah) unto my son mourning",
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַבֵּינוּ שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי מִמִּדְרָשׁ: גֵּיהִנָּם,
— which Rashi expounds from the Midrash as Gehinnom,
שֶׁהָיָה מָסוּר בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁאִם לֹא יָמוּת אֶחָד מִבָּנָיו בְּחַיָּיו אֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה פְּנֵי גֵּיהִנָּם;
— having received a divine sign that if none of his sons died during his lifetime, he was assured never to behold the face of Gehinnom;
וּכְשֶׁאֵירַע לוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה זוֹ בְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁהָיָה אָהוּב לוֹ מִכָּל בָּנָיו, הָיָה נִדְמֶה לוֹ שֶׁחָלִילָה אָבְדָה תִּקְוָתוֹ מִכֹּל וָכֹל.
— and when this catastrophe struck Joseph, his beloved son, it seemed to him that his eternal hope had vanished, Heaven forbid.

p: וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, מח עַמּוּד ב וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)
— And it is taught in the holy Zohar (Part I, 48b and elsewhere)
שֶׁקְּדוּשַׁת נַיָיחָא שֶׁל שַׁבָּת פּוֹעֵל לְהָסִיר הָעֶצֶב וְהָרוֹגֶז,
— that the holy rest of Shabbat operates to banish sorrow (etzev) and turmoil (rogez),
כִּדְכְתִיב: "בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ ה' לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ וּמֵרָגְזֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה יד, ג),
— as it is written: "in the day that Hashem shall give you rest from your sorrow, and from your turmoil, etc.",
וְדָרַשׁ עַל הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא יוֹם הָנִיחַ.
— expounding this regarding Shabbat, which is the day of divine rest.
וְעִנְיַן "עִצָּבוֹן" מַשְׁמָעוֹ עַל דְּאָגָה מִדָּבָר שֶׁעָבַר,
— Now "sorrow" (itzavon) denotes grief over what has already occurred in the past,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "נֶעֱצַב הַמֶּלֶךְ עַל בְּנוֹ" (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יט, ג) וְכַדּוֹמֶה בַּמִּקְרָא;
— as in: "the king grieved for his son";
וְעִנְיַן "רוֹגֶז" הוּא מַה שֶּׁמְּפַחֵד הָאָדָם וְחָרֵד מִדָּבָר הֶעָתִיד לָבֹא עָלָיו,
— whereas "turmoil" (rogez) denotes dread and anxiety regarding what may transpire in the future,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שָׁמְעוּ עַמִּים יִרְגָּזוּן" (שְׁמוֹת טו, יד).
— as in: "The peoples have heard, they tremble (yirgazun)".

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Vayigash 4:10: “We find that Joseph said three expressions to them: ‘do not be grieved,’ ‘let it not burn in your eyes,’ and ‘do not be agitated on the way.’ When we examine the language: grief (etzev) falls upon the past, as in ‘the king grieved for his son’; burning upon the present, as with Cain, ‘Cain was very incensed,’ for they are still engaged in the same matter; and agitation (rogez) upon the future, as in ‘the peoples heard, they trembled.’ We find three such expressions in a single verse as well, which the holy Zohar (48b) expounds regarding Shabbat: ‘On the day that Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow, from your agitation, and from the hard labor that was laid upon you’—‘from your sorrow’ for the past, ‘from your agitation’ for the future, and ‘from the hard labor’ for the present. That is, the rest and delight of Shabbat must be such that one does not remember at all, neither past nor future nor present. He should cleave so to the love and delight of Shabbat that it is as if he were above time, and past, future and present are one to him.”

p: וְהִנֵּה קְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת כִּבְרִיָּיתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הָיָה לְהוֹפִיעַ וּלְתַקֵּן אֶת שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָבְרוּ,
— Now the sanctity of Shabbat at the Creation was designed to radiate and rectify the preceding six working days,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד וְגוֹמֵר, וַיְכַל אֱלֹהִים בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, לא; ב, ב);
— as it is written: "And God saw everything that He had made, and, behold, it was very good... and on the seventh day God finished His work which He had made";
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוֹפִיעַ קְדוּשַׁת הַשַּׁבָּת לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים שֶׁעָבְרוּ בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ "טוֹב מְאֹד".
— meaning that the holiness of Shabbat shone forth to elevate all past deeds of the week into "very good."
וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת הַנְּיָיחָא "מֵעָצְבְּךָ" –
— And this is the aspect of rest "from your sorrow"—
שֶׁבְּכָל שַׁבָּת נִמְצָא קְדוּשָּׁה זוֹ לְתַקֵּן הָעֶצֶב מִכָּל מַה שֶּׁאֵירַע בְּכָל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָבְרוּ.
— for within every Shabbat abides this power to heal the sorrow over whatever occurred during the preceding week.
וְאֵצֶל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן הָיָה הַשַּׁבָּת קוֹדֶם יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
— And for Adam the First, Shabbat occurred prior to his workdays,
כִּי מִיָּד נִכְנַס לְשַׁבָּת
— for immediately upon his creation on Friday afternoon he entered Shabbat,
כְּדֵי שֶׁהַשַּׁבָּת יוֹפִיעַ בִּקְדוּשָׁתוֹ עַל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַבָּאִים;
— so that Shabbat might project its holiness onto the upcoming six workdays;
וְזֶהוּ לְהָנִיחַ "מֵרָגְזֶךָ",
— and this is rest "from your turmoil",
שֶׁמִּזֶּה נִמְצָא בְּכָל שַׁבָּת הַכֹּחַ לְהוֹפִיעַ קְדוּשָּׁה לִימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאַחֲרָיו, לְהִנָּצֵל מִפַּחַד וְרוֹגֶז.
— granting every Shabbat the power to infuse holiness into the subsequent days, delivering man from anxiety and future dread.

p: וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר הָרֶמֶז בָּזֶה בַּמִּשְׁנָה (שַׁבָּת עג עַמּוּד א):
— And one may explain the hint in the Mishnah (Shabbat 73a):
"אֲבוֹת מְלָאכוֹת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת" –
— “The primary categories of labor are forty minus one”—
וְלִכְאוֹרָה: מַה לוֹ לְהַזְכִּיר מִנְיַן אַרְבָּעִים, הֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר "שְׁלֹשִׁים וְתֵשַׁע" (וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִקְשָׁה הַתּוֹסְפוֹת יוֹם טוֹב)?
— why formulate it as "forty minus one" rather than simply "thirty-nine" (as the Tosafot Yom Tov asks)?

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 73a: “We learned in a mishna: The primary categories of labor are forty-less-one, and we discussed it and asked: Why do I need this tally of forty-less-one? And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The tally was included to teach that if one performed all of the prohibited labors in the course of one lapse of awareness during which he was unaware of the prohibition involved, he is liable for each and every one. Granted, according to Abaye, who said that in a case like that one mentioned above, where one intended to throw an object two cubits and it traveled four cubits he is liable, you find that circumstance in a case where he was aware that the prohibition of Shabbat applies to certain labors, and he was aware that particular labors were prohibited, and was mistaken with regard to measures. He intended to perform an act involving less than the prohibited measure, and it turned out that the action he performed involved an amount equal to or greater than the prohibited measure. That is an unwitting act that renders him liable to bring a sin-offering, according to Abaye. However, according to Rava, who said that he is exempt in a case where one intended to throw an object two cubits and it traveled four cubits, in what circumstances do you find that he would be liable for each and every one? Is it in a case where, with regard to Shabbat, his actions were intentional, and, with regard to the prohibited labors, his actions were unwitting?”

p: וְיוּבַן עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת מט עַמּוּד ב):
— And it will be understood based on Shabbat (49b):
שֶׁל"ט (שְׁלֹשִׁים וָתֵשַׁע) מְלָאכוֹת כְּנֶגֶד "מְלָאכָה", "מְלַאכְתּוֹ", וּ"מְלֶאכֶת" שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת.
— that the 39 labors correspond to the 39 times the words melakhah appear in the Torah.
וּבָעֵי רַב יוֹסֵף:
— And Rav Yosef inquired:
אִם "וְהַמְּלָאכָה הָיְתָה דַיָּם" (שְׁמוֹת לו, ז) מִמִּנְיָנָא הוּא,
— is "and the work was sufficient" counted among the 39,
וְ"וַיָּבֹא הַבַּיְתָה לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לט, יא) לָאו מִמִּנְיָנָא – וּכְמַאן דְּאָמַר (סוֹטָה לו עַמּוּד ב) לַעֲשׂוֹת צְרָכָיו נִכְנַס;
— and "and he went into the house to do his work" excluded, following the view that Joseph entered to satisfy his desires;
אוֹ דִילְמָא "וַיָּבֹא הַבַּיְתָה לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ" מִמִּנְיָנָא הוּא,
— or perhaps "he went into the house to do his work" is counted as literal labor,
וְהַאי "וְהַמְּלָאכָה הָיְתָה דַיָּם" הָכִי קָאָמַר: דִּשְׁלִים לֵיהּ עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— and "the work was sufficient" merely means that the craftsmanship was finished, see there.

h: The Mystery of the Fortieth Labor

p: וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ מִסְפַּר אַרְבָּעִים מְלָאכוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה:
— Meaning that there are in truth forty mentions of melakhah in the Torah:
וְל"ט מֵהֶם הֵמָּה נֶגֶד ל"ט מְלָאכוֹת שֶׁל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,
— thirty-nine corresponding to the creative labors of the six workdays,
שֶׁהֵם נִקְרָאִים "יְמֵי מְלָאכָה" שֶׁנְּתוּנִים לָאָדָם לַעֲמוֹל בִּמְלַאכְתּוֹ וּלְקַדְּשָׁם בְּכַוָּנָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
— assigned to man to sanctify with holy intention,
כִּמְלֶאכֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן שֶׁהֵם בְּמִסְפַּר ל"ט,
— mirroring the 39 labors of the Tabernacle,
שֶׁעַל זֶה הָיָה מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, כו),
— this was the intention in creating the six workdays, as it is written, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”;
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים.
— that the divine presence abide through human activity.
וְאַחַר הַחֵטְא סִילְּקוּ אֶת הַשְּׁכִינָה מֵהָאָרֶץ עַד רָקִיעַ שְׁבִיעִי,
— And after the sin of Adam, the Shechinah was removed to the seventh heaven,
עַד שֶׁבְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה הוֹרִיד מֹשֶׁה הַשְּׁכִינָה לָאָרֶץ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יט, ז);
— until at Sinai Moses brought the Shechinah back to earth (Bereishit Rabbah 19:7);
וְאַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל צִוָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת הַמִּשְׁכָּן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עַל כָּל פָּנִים הַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה בְּמָקוֹם מְיוּחָד,
— and after the corruption, Hashem commanded the building of the Tabernacle so that the Shechinah would at least rest in a designated place,
וְאָז נִגְמְרוּ הַל"ט מְלָאכוֹת שֶׁבַּמִּשְׁכָּן.
— wherein the 39 labors were consummated.
וּקְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת הַמְּנוּחָה נֶחְשָׁב גַּם כֵּן לִמְלָאכָה,
— And the holy rest of Shabbat is itself counted as a creative act,
הַסּוֹכֵם מִסְפָּר שֶׁל אַרְבָּעִים מְלָאכוֹת שֶׁנִּרְמַז בַּתּוֹרָה.
— completing the full tally of forty labors hinted in the Torah.

p: וְהִנֵּה אוֹתוֹ מַאן דְּאָמַר דְּ"וַיָּבֹא הַבַּיְתָה לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ" – מְלַאכְתּוֹ מַמָּשׁ, וְהוּא מִמִּנְיַן ל"ט מְלָאכוֹת,
— Now according to the authority who holds that Joseph's "work" was literal labor, belonging to the 39,
מִמֵּילָא "וְהַמְּלָאכָה הָיְתָה דַיָּם" הוּא נֶגֶד מְלָאכָה הָאַרְבָּעִים שֶׁל שַׁבָּת,
— then "and the work was sufficient" represents the fortieth labor of Shabbat,
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר דִּשְׁלִים לֵיהּ עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ:
— meaning that the work was brought to completion:
וְהַיְינוּ בְּעֶצֶם הַמְּלָאכָה שֶׁל שַׁבָּת, שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בָּהּ כָּל הַמְּלָאכוֹת שֶׁל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָבְרוּ לִהְיוֹת נִתְקָנִים כִּמְלֶאכֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן;
— namely the essential labor of Shabbat, wherein all past weekday labors are completed and rectified like the Tabernacle;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיְכַל אֱלֹהִים בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה",
— as written: "And on the seventh day God finished His work which He had made",
וְהוּא בְּעֶצֶם הַמְּלָאכָה שֶׁל שַׁבָּת דִּשְׁלִים לֵיהּ עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ שֶׁל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
— Shabbat itself completing the work of the six days.
וְזֶהוּ אֶחָד מֵהַדְּבָרִים שֶׁשִּׁינּוּ לְתַלְמַי הַמֶּלֶךְ, שֶׁכָּתְבוּ: "וַיְכַל בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי" (מְגִילָּה ט עַמּוּד א),
— And this was one of the alterations made for King Ptolemy (Megillah 9a): writing "and He finished on the sixth day",
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם הַשָּׂגָה לְהַרְגִּישׁ שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֶצֶם מְלַאכְתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיְּתוּקְּנוּ שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָבְרוּ,
— for the pagans could not fathom that Shabbat rest is itself God's creative finishing stroke;
וְזֶה שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י שָׁם: שֶׁהוּא לֹא יְקַבֵּל מִדְרַשׁ חֲכָמִים: "מַה הָיָה הָעוֹלָם חָסֵר? מְנוּחָה, בָּאת שַׁבָּת בָּאת מְנוּחָה, וְזֶהוּ גְּמָרוֹ".
— as Rashi explains: Ptolemy would reject the Sages' teaching: "What was the world lacking? Rest; when Shabbat arrived, rest arrived, and the creation was finished".
וּלְזֶה נִקְרְאוּ "שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין לח עַמּוּד א) עַל פָּסוּק "חָצְבָה עַמּוּדֶיהָ שִׁבְעָה" (מִשְׁלֵי ט, א) – אֵלּוּ שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית,
— Therefore they are termed the "seven days of Creation", as in Sanhedrin (38a): "She has hewn out her seven pillars—these are the seven days of Creation",
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבְּשֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה חָסֵר מְנוּחָה, עַד שֶׁבָּא שַׁבָּת בָּא מְנוּחָה.
— for as Tosafot noted, although the physical world was made in six days, it lacked rest until Shabbat completed it.
וְעַל כֵּן הַשַּׁבָּת גַּם כֵּן מֵהַמִּנְיָן שֶׁהִשְׁלִים אֶת הַמְּלָאכָה,
— Hence Shabbat is part of the count that finished the work,
וְזֶה מְרַמֵּז עַל "יוֹם הָנִיחַ לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ" – לְתַקֵּן הָעֶצֶב שֶׁל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָבְרוּ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
— alluding to "the day Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow"—rectifying the past week.

p: וְאִי נֵימָא דְּפָסוּק "וְהַמְּלָאכָה הָיְתָה דַיָּם" מִמִּנְיָנָא הוּא – מִמִּנְיַן הַל"ט מְלָאכוֹת,
— And if we say that "and the work was sufficient" is counted among the 39,
וּמִמֵּילָא "וַיָּבֹא הַבַּיְתָה לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ" כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר לַעֲשׂוֹת צְרָכָיו נִכְנַס,
— so that "he went into the house to do his work" follows the view that he entered for desire,
נִמְצָא שֶׁזֶּהוּ סוֹכֵם לְמִנְיַן אַרְבָּעִים הַמְּרַמֵּז לִמְלֶאכֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
— then this becomes the fortieth, alluding to the work of Shabbat.
דְּהִנֵּה בֶּאֱמֶת אֵין לוֹ הֲבָנָה עַל פִּי פְּשׁוּטוֹ שֶׁיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק יִהְיֶה נִפְתֶּה חָלִילָה אַף לְפִי שָׁעָה עַל מַעֲשֶׂה כָּזוֹ בַּפּוֹעַל!
— For in truth, it is unthinkable according to literal peshat that Joseph the Righteous would be seduced, Heaven forbid, even for a moment into actual transgression!
אָמְנָם, הֲגַם שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי שֶׁבְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה הָיָה לוֹ מִלְחָמָה לַעֲמוֹד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן,
— Rather, although he certainly experienced an intense battle to withstand the trial,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בְּשֵׁם הָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ רַבִּי רַבִּי בּוּנִם זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה
— as they cite in the name of the holy master Rebbe Bunim, of blessed memory,
עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סוֹטָה יא עַמּוּד ב):
— on what is taught in Sotah (11b):
"'וַתִּירֶאןָ הַמְיַלְּדֹת אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים וְלֹא עָשׂוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אֲלֵיהֶן וְגוֹמֵר' (שְׁמוֹת א, יז) – מְלַמֵּד שֶׁתְּבָעָן לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה וְלֹא נִתְבְּעוּ",
— on the Hebrew midwives: "Pharaoh solicited them for sin, but they were not receptive",
שֶׁדִּקְדְּקוּ בִּלְשׁוֹנָם הַצַּח: "וְלֹא נִתְבְּעוּ",
— noting the pure phrasing: "they were not receptive",
שֶׁלָּשׁוֹן זֶה יוֹרֶה שֶׁלֹּא בָּא בְּלִבָּם שׁוּם הֶרְגֵּשׁ תַּאֲוָה לָזֶה שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִתְבָּעִים;
— showing that not the slightest stirring of desire arose within their hearts;
אֲבָל בְּיוֹסֵף כְּתִיב לְשׁוֹן "וַיְמָאֵן" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לט, ח),
— whereas regarding Joseph Scripture uses the word "and he refused" (va-yema'en),
הַיְינוּ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה לוֹ הֶרְגֵּשׁ תַּאֲוָה בְּלִבּוֹ, רַק שֶׁהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ לַעֲמוֹד בַּנִּסָּיוֹן.
— meaning that desire did stir in his heart, but he heroically conquered his inclination to overcome the trial.

p: וְהַיְינוּ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פה, ב):
— And this is understood based on Bereishit Rabbah (85:2):
שֶׁאִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל פּוֹטִיפַר לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם נִתְכַּוְּונָה, שֶׁרוֹאָה הָיְתָה בָּאַצְטַגְנִינוּת שֶׁלָּהּ שֶׁהִיא עֲתִידָה לְהַעֲמִיד מִמֶּנּוּ בֵּן וְכוּלֵי;
— that Potiphar's wife acted for the sake of Heaven, seeing in her astrological visions that she was destined to produce children through him (which was fulfilled through her daughter Asenath);
וּמִכָּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק רָאָה זֹאת בְּוַדַּאי שֶׁעָתִיד לְהַעֲמִיד מְנַשֶּׁה וְאֶפְרַיִם מִבִּתָּהּ.
— and all the more so did Joseph the Righteous foresee that he was destined to father Manasseh and Ephraim from her daughter!
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַאֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה "לַעֲשׂוֹת צְרָכָיו נִכְנַס":
— And this is what the Sages meant by "he entered to do his needs":
כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁזֶּה עִיקַּר מִדַּת יוֹסֵף, שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַשְׁפָּעַת הַבְּרָכָה לִכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— for this is the essence of Joseph (Yesod), channeling divine blessing to all Israel,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיְכַלְכֵּל יוֹסֵף וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית מז, יב);
— as written: "And Joseph nourished his father and his brothers, etc.";
וְלָכֵן הוֹלִיד אֶת אֶפְרַיִם שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרְאוּ עַל שְׁמוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הֲבֵן יַקִּיר לִי אֶפְרַיִם" (יִרְמְיָה לא, יט).
— fathering Ephraim after whom all Israel are named: "Is Ephraim My dear son?"
וְזֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ הָיָה גּוֹדֶל הַנִּסָּיוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ:
— And this constituted the supreme depth of his trial:
שֶׁנִּדְמָה לוֹ לְפִי שָׁעָה שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה מִצְוָה בָּזֶה,
— that it seemed to him momentarily that he would be fulfilling a holy mitzvah,
וְזֶהוּ "לַעֲשׂוֹת צְרָכָיו" – מַה שֶּׁמּוּטָל עָלָיו בְּחִינַת יְסוֹד, לְהוֹלִיד אֶת אֶפְרַיִם,
— to fulfill his cosmic role in Yesod to father Ephraim,
שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַשְׁפָּעָה לִכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ הָאוֹר,
— channeling the divine light to all Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אוֹר זָרֻעַ לַצַּדִּיק" (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא),
— as written: "Light is sown for the righteous",
וּכְתִיב: "וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ד), וְאֵין "טוֹב" אֶלָּא צַדִּיק שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב" (יְשַׁעְיָה ג, י; חֲגִיגָה יב עַמּוּד א).
— and "God saw the light that it was good," and "good" is the Tzaddik (Chagigah 12a).
כִּי כֵּן דֶּרֶךְ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, לְהַרְאוֹת בְּעֵת הַנִּסָּיוֹן שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה מִצְוָה בָּזֶה,
— For such is the cunning of the yetzer hara: to portray at the moment of temptation that the act is a pious mitzvah,
וּכְמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שָׂמִים חֹשֶׁךְ לְאוֹר" (יְשַׁעְיָה ה, כ).
— putting darkness for light.
אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּרְאָה לוֹ דְּמוּת דִּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו (סוֹטָה לו עַמּוּד ב),
— Until the visage of his father Jacob appeared to him (Sotah 36b),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבָּזֶה נִזְכַּר בְּעַצְמוֹ עַל יְדֵי דִּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ אֱמֶת,
— meaning that through Jacob's visage, whose attribute is absolute Truth,
וּמִמֵּילָא עָמַד עַל הָאֱמֶת שֶׁהוּא הֲסָתָה שֶׁל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בַּשֶּׁקֶר וְאֵין לוֹ קִיּוּם.
— Joseph realized the truth: that this was a deceitful seduction of the yetzer hara which has no endurance.

p: וְנִמְצָא דִּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר "לַעֲשׂוֹת צְרָכָיו נִכְנַס", "מְלַאכְתּוֹ" מְרַמֵּז גַּם כֵּן עַל מְלֶאכֶת שַׁבָּת,
— Thus, according to the view that he entered to fulfill his needs, his "work" likewise alludes to the work of Shabbat,
שֶׁהוּא סוֹכֵם מִסְפַּר הָאַרְבָּעִים,
— completing the sum of forty,
שֶׁהוּא בְּעֶצֶם מְלֶאכֶת שַׁבָּת: שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַשְׁפָּעַת הַבְּרָכָה,
— which is the essential labor of Shabbat: the source of all blessing,
מִבּוּעָא דְּבֵירָא, לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ הָאוֹר שֶׁל מִדַּת יְסוֹד,
— the flowing wellspring radiating the light of Yesod,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "מָה רַב טוּבְךָ אֲשֶׁר צָפַנְתָּ לִּירֵאֶיךָ" (תְּהִלִּים לא, כ).
— as written: "How abundant is Your goodness, which You have laid up for them that fear You".
וְהָאוֹר הַזֶּה נִתְגַּלָּה בִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
— And this light is unveiled in the sanctity of Shabbat,
לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ שֶׁפַע וּבְרָכָה לְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַבָּאִים,
— channeling blessing into the upcoming six workdays,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, סג עַמּוּד ב): "כָּל שִׁיתָא יוֹמִין מִתְבָּרְכָאן מִיּוֹמָא שְׁבִיעָאָה".
— "all six days are blessed from the seventh day."
וּבְחִינַת מְלָאכָה זוֹ שֶׁל שַׁבָּת מְרוּמָּז עַל "הָנִיחַ מֵרָגְזֶךָ" –
— And this dimension of Shabbat labor alludes to rest "from your turmoil"—
שֶׁהִיא הַנְּיָיחָא לְבַל לִרְגּוֹז וְלִפְחוֹד מִקִּלְקוּל שֶׁל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַבָּאִים,
— which is the serenity that removes fear of stumbling during the upcoming weekdays,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקְּדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת מַשְׁפִּיעַ בָּהֶם קְדוּשָּׁה וְשֶׁפַע בְּרָכָה.
— because the sanctity of Shabbat infuses them with blessing.
וְעַל רֶמֶז זֶה נִרְמַז בְּפָסוּק "וַיָּבֹא הַבַּיְתָה לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ",
— And to this alludes the verse: "and he went into the house to do his work",
שֶׁהוּא רָגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף שֶׁנֶּהְפַּךְ הַכֹּל אַחַר כָּךְ לְטוֹב:
— which was the turmoil of Joseph, wherein everything was ultimately transformed into good:
